title: Quantity workshop
question: Can you select a bounded expression whose dimension matches the target without mistaking that match for equal quantity kind?
predictionPrompt: Choose a target and predict the result before the dimension trace appears. The unlike-addition preset is deliberately invalid: try to explain why no conversion can rescue it.
sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure 2026 update; JCGM 200:2012; NIST SP 811e2008
sourceLocator: BIPM sections 2.2-2.3; VIM3 entries 1.2, 1.7, 1.19-1.21; NIST SP 811 chapter 8 and Appendix B
caveats: A dimension match is necessary but not sufficient for equal quantity kind or empirical validity.
NIST SP 811 predates the International System of Units (SI) changes effective 20 May 2019 and is used only for notation and conversion guidance.

numericalMethod.name: Rational dimension-exponent arithmetic
numericalMethod.description: The source contract specifies exact rational exponent addition, subtraction, and equality; the current activity inputs are restricted to integer exponents.

modelComponents.label: International System of Quantities dimension arithmetic
modelComponents.description: Combines quantity dimensions as products of powers over the seven conventional base quantities of the International System of Quantities (ISQ).

attribution.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; JCGM 200:2012
caveats: The seven-axis basis is conventional and the activity inputs use only integer exponents.

modelComponents.label: Multiplicative International System of Units and mechanical centimetre-gram-second conversion
modelComponents.description: Converts a target-bound canonical International System of Units (SI) quantity value to declared mechanical centimetre-gram-second (CGS) coordinates.

attribution.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; NIST SP 811e2008
attribution.sourceLocator: BIPM section 2.3; NIST SP 811 chapter 8 and Appendix B
caveats: Electromagnetic CGS and affine temperature conversions are excluded.

equations: A + B is defined only for quantities of the same kind; then dim(A + B) = dim(A) = dim(B)
assumptions: The Tour uses seven conventional International System of Quantities (ISQ) base-quantity dimensions rather than seven intrinsic dimensions.
The general dimension type permits rational exponents; every expression in this activity uses integer exponents.
The optional sample magnitude is the selected target's canonical SI quantity value, not a second independent expression magnitude.
Coordinate conversion is limited to multiplicative coherent scaling between SI and mechanical-cgs units of the selected target kind.
Electromagnetic CGS conventions and affine temperature conversions are explicitly excluded.
The exercise checks a dimension contract and does not compare with empirical evidence.

controls.label: Target quantity kind
controls.description: Selects the target quantity kind, dimension, canonical International System of Units (SI) unit, and mechanical centimetre-gram-second (CGS) unit.
controls.playfulPrompt: Pick the quantity you want the workshop to construct.

options.label: Torque
options.description: shares energy's dimension but not its quantity kind

controls.label: Named expression
controls.description: Selects one bounded expression with declared operand quantity kinds and one immediate operation.
controls.playfulPrompt: Predict the exponent trace before you reveal the result.

options.label: force x path length
options.description: energy dimension; quantity kind still requires context

controls.label: Unit coordinates
controls.description: Selects International System of Units (SI) or mechanical centimetre-gram-second (CGS) coordinates for the target-bound quantity value.
controls.playfulPrompt: Change the coordinate language without changing the target quantity value.

options.label: International System of Units (SI)
options.description: canonical SI unit for the selected target

options.label: Mechanical centimetre-gram-second (CGS)
options.description: centimetre, gram, and second scaling only; electromagnetic CGS excluded

controls.label: Target value in its canonical SI unit
controls.description: Supplies one numerical value bound to the selected target quantity kind and canonical SI unit for multiplicative coordinate conversion.
controls.playfulPrompt: Follow one target-bound quantity value as only its numerical value and unit change.

presets.label: Race the clock
presets.description: Construct average speed from path length and elapsed time.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Can you predict L T^-1 before revealing the trace?

presets.label: Push a mass
presets.description: Construct the force dimension from mass and acceleration.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Which exponents combine when the two quantities multiply?

presets.label: Same dimension, different kind
presets.description: Match the torque target with a force-times-length expression and inspect the quantity-kind caveat.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Will a dimension match alone tell you whether the expression denotes energy or torque?

presets.label: Break the equation
presets.description: Try adding a path length to elapsed time and inspect why the operation is undefined.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Predict whether any multiplicative unit conversion can rescue this sum.

outputSchema.label: Operation status
outputSchema.description: Reports defined for a valid bounded operation or undefined-unlike-addition for the deliberately invalid sum; this is distinct from provenance resultStatus.

outputSchema.label: Result dimension
outputSchema.description: Seven-axis rational-exponent vector; null when the selected operation is undefined. This activity emits integer-valued exponents.

outputSchema.label: Target dimension
outputSchema.description: Seven-axis rational-exponent vector declared for the selected target quantity kind.

outputSchema.label: Target dimension match
outputSchema.description: True only when the defined result dimension equals the target dimension; it does not assert equal quantity kind.

outputSchema.label: Quantity-kind caveat
outputSchema.description: Explains that dimension equality is necessary but insufficient for quantity-kind identity, including the energy/torque case.

outputSchema.label: Target numerical value
outputSchema.description: Converted numerical value of the target-bound canonical SI quantity value; null when the operation is undefined or its dimension misses the target.

outputSchema.label: Target unit
outputSchema.description: Declared SI or mechanical-cgs unit for coordinateValue; null whenever coordinateValue is null.

comparison.incompatibleBehavior: Render parallel findings without a residual or merged quantity when compatibility keys differ.

visualization.description: Shows operand, result, and target exponents by declared dimension axis, plus the target-bound coordinate conversion.

alternatives.description: A sentence reports operation status, exponent arithmetic, target match, coordinate value and unit, and the quantity-kind caveat.
A table lists each declared dimension axis with operand, result, and target exponents, followed by coordinate fields.

visualization.reducedMotionBehavior: Render the final trace immediately without animated exponent movement.

finding.changed: At runtime, the result trace is specified to respond to the target, named expression, and coordinate system; Technical depth also exposes one target-bound SI numerical value.
finding.cause: Quantities multiply or divide while dimension exponents add or subtract; valid multiplicative unit changes rescale only the target quantity's numerical value.
assumptions: The named expression's operand quantity kinds are declared correctly
The selected target's SI and mechanical-cgs units use a multiplicative coherent scale
No quantity-kind identity is inferred from dimension equality
finding.establishes: For an evaluated run, whether one bounded named expression has the selected target dimension in the declared ISQ basis, and the coordinate representation of one target-bound quantity value when applicable.
finding.doesNotEstablish: That the expression has the target quantity kind, is an empirically correct law, reproduces an external result, or agrees with a dataset.
finding.sourceLocator: VIM3 entries 1.2, 1.7, and 1.19-1.21; NIST SP 811 chapter 8 and Appendix B
caveats: No external result or empirical dataset is reproduced or compared.
Electromagnetic CGS and affine temperature conversions are outside the contract.
